title: Advanced Pipelining Patterns in CuTe DSL
critical_patterns: Double Buffering: Alternate between two buffers to load and compute simultaneously.
Triple Buffering: Use three or more buffers for maximum overlap.
Warp-Specialized Pipeline: Dedicate warps to loading and computing separately.
Async Copy Patterns: Use hardware-accelerated async copy for efficient data transfer.
TMA Pipeline: Use Hopper's Tensor Memory Accelerator with transaction-based pipelining.

constraints: Use 3-4 stages for most cases to balance resource usage and performance.
Ensure NUM_STAGES * stage_size is less than maximum shared memory.
Avoid over-pipelining as it can lead to reduced occupancy and performance.
Synchronize correctly to avoid race conditions and ensure data readiness.
Pipeline only memory-bound kernels; compute-bound kernels may not benefit.
compressed_summary: Pipelining in CuTe DSL involves overlapping data movement with computation to hide memory latency, enhancing performance. Key patterns include double buffering, which uses two buffers to load and compute simultaneously, and triple buffering, which employs three or more buffers for deeper pipelining. Warp specialization separates loading and computing tasks across different warps, improving parallelism. Async copy patterns leverage hardware-accelerated operations for efficient data transfer, while TMA pipelining on Hopper utilizes transaction-based synchronization for optimal performance. Effective pipelining requires careful stage management, typically using 3-4 stages to balance latency hiding and resource constraints. Over-pipelining can lead to reduced occupancy, so it's crucial to measure and tune pipeline depth based on specific kernel characteristics. Synchronization points must be correctly placed to prevent race conditions. Pipelining is particularly beneficial for memory-bound kernels, offering 1.5-3× speedup by keeping the GPU busy and minimizing idle time. The document emphasizes the importance of profiling to determine the optimal pipeline configuration and warns against exceeding shared memory limits or improperly synchronizing stages. For further optimization, related topics such as tiling strategies and thread layouts are recommended.
